_comment: Every utterance here is one that REACHES THE PLANNER. Commands handled by
the voice rule fast path (get_time, stop, and the nine system tools in
trigger.py::_VOICE_FAST_PATH_TOOLS) are deliberately absent: benching them
would measure the rule engine, not the model.
`accept` is a LIST because several of these are genuinely ambiguous between
sibling tools. A case with one entry is a case where exactly one answer is
defensible; a case with two is one where the bench refuses to punish a
reasonable pick. Arg VALUES are matched as case-insensitive substrings so
'Tokyo' matches 'tokyo, japan'. A null value means 'any value, but the arg
expect: 'tool' = at least one tool call. 'none' = the planner should answer

cases.utterance: open spotify
what's the weather in Tokyo
play some lofi hip hop
remind me in 10 minutes to check the oven
send Sharath a whatsapp saying I'll be late
translate good morning into Japanese
who won the last cricket world cup
cases.note: Wants an answer out loud, not links. search_and_answer per its own docstring.

cases.utterance: show me search results for mechanical keyboards
cases.note: Explicitly asked to SHOW a search -> the browser-window tool.

cases.utterance: find me some links about rust async runtimes
cases.note: Genuinely ambiguous; both defensible. Accepts either.

cases.utterance: what's the forecast looking like this week
what's Apple trading at right now
any tech news today
cases.note: The two news tools name the SAME concept differently — get_news takes `category`, get_news_data takes `topic`. This case originally demanded `category` from whichever tool was picked, so all six models were marked wrong for correctly calling get_news_data(topic=...). The sibling inconsistency is a real defect; scoring it here was a fixture bug.

cases.utterance: remember that my cat is named Luna
cases.note: Accepts BOTH deliberately. `remember`'s docstring uses this exact sentence as its example, but take_note's claims every 'remember that' request. Scoring it strict would measure a tool-description defect and report it as a model difference. The overlap is a real bug — fix the descriptions, don't grade the model on them.

cases.utterance: note down that the router password is hunter2
cases.note: Accepts either — the two tool descriptions genuinely overlap here.

cases.utterance: find my resume and read it out to me
cases.note: Step 2 (read_file) needs step 1's path, so the FIRST call must be find_file. This is the case approach A exists for.

cases.utterance: what's on my screen right now
open chrome and spotify
cases.note: Two calls expected. Tests whether the planner batches or drops one.

cases.utterance: open notepad, chrome and firefox
cases.note: Trips Guardian's fan-out brake downstream (MAX_UNCONFIRMED_SIDE_EFFECTS=2), but the PLANNER should still emit three.

cases.utterance: open notepad and remind me in 5 minutes to save my work
cases.note: Two different tools in one utterance.

cases.utterance: search youtube for python tutorials
cases.note: search_web takes an `engine` arg; a hallucinated `site`/`platform` arg fails the argname check.

cases.utterance: show me a map of Paris
read the file C:/temp/notes.txt
cases.note: Arg is `path`, not `file`/`filename`/`filepath` — the classic hallucination.

cases.utterance: summarize https://example.com/article
find any file with budget in the name
delete the file C:/temp/old.txt
cases.note: delete_file's parameter really is `file`, not `path` — this originally demanded `path` and marked every model wrong for being right. The planner SHOULD emit this; Guardian is what holds it for confirmation, so a refusal here is a planner failure, not safety.

cases.utterance: shut down the pc
hey there
thanks, that's great
what kinds of things can you do
send a message
cases.note: planner.py's own rule: ask for the missing parameters via final_response rather than guessing a contact.
